trials.diagnosis: Passed all hidden groups. The solver used a co-rotating critical-state propagation with a shot through the conducting contact and integrated the lifted normal electric field.

The submitted solver discarded the threading polarity in the cross-plane voltage and Hall law, and selected the substrate induction at the discontinuous sheet on the equality case. The signed induction fixes the electric readouts; taking the specified coating-side magnetic trace also fixes induction.

The unthreaded model assumed the dilute constant-winding similarity solution throughout a layer with field-dependent critical current. The normal voltage omitted the entire active substrate interval for probes reaching the core. Using the submission’s own critical-field propagator at n=0, retaining the regular weak seed, and integrating the active substrate up to the front fixes both discrepancies.

physical_failure_review.criteria: Three fresh unhinted Luna High completions on the same frozen revision. All agents and verifiers finished without exceptions, all submissions passed public and private calibration, and only private observable-prediction checks failed. Correcting the identified physics at the submitted parameter or isolating it from numerical error confirms the diagnosis.
physical_failure_review.timing: Wall times come from native Harbor records. Where macOS recorded host sleep, host-awake elapsed time subtracts overlapping sleep intervals (second-resolution host log).

At zero interface E the substrate is screened, but the submission replaced the superconducting film by a finite-conductance bare sheet. It also used the wrong lift of the corner normal and took the absolute value of the threading field in the DC voltage. Replacing just the failed shooting branch by the shielded coating solution fixes tangential fields and power at fixed pinning. Using the signed lifted critical normal also fixes the voltage.

On the smooth depinning cylinder the current was normalized using the tangential projection of E and augmented by an incorrectly projected parallel term. This violates both the true critical-current norm and work-maximizing direction when the cutting plane is inactive. Keeping its film, shooting, normal-flux and integration code, and correcting the smooth-cylinder support recovers induction, tangential E and power. It additionally set the voltage integral to zero when the probe reached the pinned core. Keeping its through-layer integral fixes the voltage.

The submission propagated a spatially constant depinning threshold equal to its value at the threading field and omitted the azimuthal reversal of magnetic induction. At a cutting corner its transverse projection omitted the x component of the perpendicular basis. On the smooth face it computed the required parallel current for Jx=0 but omitted that contribution when returning the tangential current. Restoring these physical relations at the submitted fitted pinning recovers the registered film probes.
